title: Warm pool supervises its workers: respawn off the critical path, quarantine crash loops

body:
## Summary
The warm pool treats a dead worker as a lazy problem: whichever sentence next draws it pays a full model load inline, a worker that cannot load is retried on every draw, and one bad worker at startup throws away the whole pool. Make WarmPool the supervisor of its workers: start with whatever loads (>=1), respawn a dead worker in the background the moment it dies, keep a per-worker crash budget that quarantines a crash-looping slot, and let acquire() hand out only live workers.

## Description
Leans on subprocess-lifecycle `concurrency-and-slots` (a slot must be backed by a live process - 'slots held with no live process'; the slot's reaper is the reap) and sidecar-provisioning `plugin-lazy-load-and-reload` ('a plugin process died under a live request'), with backend-platform `self-healing` for the bounded-retry/quarantine shape. Today the cost of a crash lands on the viewer: the head-of-line sentence absorbs a load the daemon's 15 s lag bound does not know about, and a permanently broken slot converts a share of every burst into `skipped: error` lines forever. Moving the load to a supervisor thread started at death makes the reload overlap useful work, the crash budget turns a crash loop into a smaller healthy pool, and a partial start keeps the warm engine instead of falling back to a model load per sentence. The hello reason gains 'N of M workers' inside the existing 'engine: warm (...)' phrase, so the daemon's readiness check is untouched.

## Flow
- Worker death (reader sees EOF, timeout kill) -> pool marks the slot respawning and starts a supervisor thread: start + ready() with backoff
- acquire(): wait on the condition for a LIVE idle worker; if every slot is quarantined, raise EngineError at once
- crash budget: K failed loads in a window -> slot quarantined, logged once to stderr with its tail
- start(): load all in parallel, keep the ones that are ready; fail only when zero load
- close(): stop supervisors, kill and reap any process mid-load

## Expected impact
A worker crash mid-show no longer puts a multi-second model load on the sentence the viewer is waiting for; a broken slot stops producing line errors; a flaky load at startup keeps the warm engine (RTF ~0.32) instead of the per-sentence binary.

## Evaluation
Claim: dead and broken workers are healed or quarantined off the critical path.
Before: 0 of 6 acceptance cases pass (partial start falls back, reload is inline, crash loop errors sentences, no quarantine, no background respawn to reap)
After: 6 of 6
Method: gate - acceptance tests written first against fake_warm with per-spawn failure and load-delay knobs
Result: better
Gate: architecture (changes the pool's lifecycle model documented in docs/guide/voice.md)

body:
## Summary
The sidecar announces which engine it runs by writing a sentence into `reason`, and the daemon decides whether the voice is ready by substring-matching that sentence. Per-sentence cost (render time, how long a rendered sentence waited for its turn, viseme time) exists in the sidecar and is printed to stderr, where the daemon throws it away. Make both typed: an `engine` object on hello and timing fields on audio, parsed by the daemon and shown by `voice say`.

## Description
Leans on voice-io `engine-abstraction`: 'callers branch on capability, never on identity', and absent / broken / ready must be distinguishable - today the daemon branches on a phrase, and 'warm failed to load, fell back' vs 'warm not installed' are both prose. Also voice-io `real-time-synthesis-budget`: an engine's speed is a measured figure, and the protocol is the one place it can be measured per sentence without scraping logs. Additive fields under protocol 1; reason keeps its words, so old daemons and old sidecars interoperate both ways. The daemon's hello_state branches on engine.kind and falls back to the substring only when the field is absent.

## Flow
- sidecar hello(): build engine = {kind: warm|process|none, workers?, load_ms?, fallback?} beside the unchanged reason
- Sidecar._speak: stamp render_ms (render.took_ms), held_ms (send time minus render done), face_ms (viseme time) on each audio line
- daemon SidecarLine::Hello gains engine: Option<EngineHello>; probe::hello_state(cfg, visemes, reason, engine)
- Rendered gains render_ms/held_ms/face_ms: Option<u32>; cli `voice say` prints them
- contract appendix documents the fields and retires 'The hello has no field for it'

## Expected impact
A wording change in the sidecar can no longer flip the voice to degraded; operators see where a sentence's latency went (render vs queue vs face) in `voice say` and replays, which is the input every later latency decision needs.

## Evaluation
Claim: engine identity and sentence cost are machine-readable on the wire.
Before: 0 of 6 acceptance cases pass (no engine field, substring decides readiness, no timing fields)
After: 6 of 6
Method: gate - acceptance tests written first (Python protocol tests, Rust on_line/hello_state tests)
Result: better
Gate: contract (daemon-private sidecar protocol in docs/spec/contract.md; additive)

critic.reason: Floor failure: an honest S (additive fields plus a parse branch) inflated to M at bare-minimum scores.
